title: Stay in control of your phone, and share your skills

say: Stay in control of your phone, and share your skills.
This is the video for module 3 of Foundational Digital Skills.
If your phone is stolen, can a stranger get in? And can you get your information back?

say: Step 1. In Settings, search Screen lock and choose a PIN of at least 6 digits.

panel.heading: Lock it and turn on Find My Device
items: Set a PIN of at least 6 digits
Turn on Find My Device and Location
Dial *#06# and write down your IMEI

say: Step 2. Avoid 123456, your birth year or your phone number.

panel.heading: Lock it and turn on Find My Device
items: Set a PIN of at least 6 digits
Turn on Find My Device and Location
Dial *#06# and write down your IMEI

say: Step 3. Hide sensitive content on the lock screen, so bank alerts and OTPs do not show.

panel.heading: Lock it and turn on Find My Device
items: Set a PIN of at least 6 digits
Turn on Find My Device and Location
Dial *#06# and write down your IMEI

say: Step 4. Turn on Find My Device and Location. From google.com/android/find on any browser, you can ring, lock or erase a lost phone.

panel.heading: Lock it and turn on Find My Device
items: Set a PIN of at least 6 digits
Turn on Find My Device and Location
Dial *#06# and write down your IMEI

say: Step 5. Dial *#06#. The screen shows your IMEI, a 15-digit number that identifies the handset. Write it on paper and keep it at home.

panel.heading: Lock it and turn on Find My Device
items: Set a PIN of at least 6 digits
Turn on Find My Device and Location
Dial *#06# and write down your IMEI

say: Erasing removes your data, so always locate and lock first.

panel.heading: Lock it and turn on Find My Device
items: Set a PIN of at least 6 digits
Turn on Find My Device and Location
Dial *#06# and write down your IMEI
panel.rule: Locate and lock first. Erase only if it is gone for good.

say: Step 1. Write exactly what happens, when, in which app, and screenshot any error.

panel.heading: The five-step troubleshooting routine

say: Step 2. Is data on? Is your bundle finished? Turn airplane mode on for ten seconds, then off, to reconnect.

panel.heading: The five-step troubleshooting routine

say: Step 3. Swipe the app away and open it again. If that fails, restart the phone.

panel.heading: The five-step troubleshooting routine

say: Step 4. Check storage. Clearing an app's cache removes temporary files and is safe.

panel.heading: The five-step troubleshooting routine

say: Step 5. Search the exact error with your phone model, and prefer official help sites. Never install unknown cleaner apps.

panel.heading: The five-step troubleshooting routine

say: Clear data is different. It resets the app and can delete your saved information, so back up first.

panel.heading: The five-step troubleshooting routine
panel.rule: Clear cache is safe. Clear data can delete your information.

say: For example, Chiamaka in Owerri could not take photos. Only 1.4 GB was free.

panel.heading: Chiamaka frees 9.7 GB

say: In WhatsApp, Manage storage, forwarded videos used 4.2 GB. She deleted them.

panel.heading: Chiamaka frees 9.7 GB

say: Files by Google removed 0.9 GB of junk and 1.1 GB of duplicate images.

panel.heading: Chiamaka frees 9.7 GB

say: Her photos were already backed up, so she freed another 3.5 GB.

panel.heading: Chiamaka frees 9.7 GB

say: In about 15 minutes she had 11.1 GB free, and lost nothing important.
But if a battery is swollen, very hot, smells of burning, or has been in water, stop. Do not charge it. Take it to a trusted repairer.

say: For example, Kemi taught her neighbour Mama Tunde in Osogbo to set a reminder. I do. Mama Tunde unlocked her own phone, and Kemi showed the steps once, slowly.

panel.heading: I do, We do, You do
items: We do: she taps, you point and name
You do: she does it alone

say: We do. Mama Tunde tapped every button while Kemi pointed and named each item.

panel.heading: I do, We do, You do
items: We do: she taps, you point and name
You do: she does it alone

say: You do. Mama Tunde made a second event on her own.

panel.heading: I do, We do, You do
items: We do: she taps, you point and name
You do: she does it alone

say: Check. Mama Tunde explained the steps back in Yoruba, in her own words.

panel.heading: I do, We do, You do
items: We do: she taps, you point and name
You do: she does it alone

say: The common mistake is taking the phone and doing it quickly yourself. Keep your hands off, and look away while she types private details.

panel.heading: I do, We do, You do
items: We do: she taps, you point and name
You do: she does it alone
panel.rule: Her phone, her hands. Never ask for her PIN or passwords.

say: To remember. Use a 6-digit PIN and turn on Find My Device. Back up before anything goes wrong. Keep your IMEI on paper. Restart first, and clear cache, not data. And teach on her phone, with your hands off.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A 6-digit PIN, and Find My Device on
Back up contacts, photos and WhatsApp
Keep your IMEI on paper at home
Restart first; clear cache, not data
Teach on her phone, with your hands off
